newsitem.title: USA: Investors put $19.5 billion into stock funds last month.
newsitem.headline: Investors put $19.5 billion into stock funds last month.

text.p: Investors poured $19.5 billion into stock mutual funds last month, down from $29.1 billion in January, the Investment Company Institute said Thursday.

Investors put another $2 billion into bond funds, which was down from $3.4 billion in January. The January figures were revised from $29.4 billion in stock funds and $2.9 bilion in bond funds, the institute said.

The institute, a trade group representing the nation's mutual fund industry, said its monthly estimates are based on a survey of long-term funds that account for about 97 percent of long-term mutual fund assets.
Bond and income flows were $2 billion in February compared with a revised $3.4 billion in January. January bond and income flows were previously reported at $2.9 billion.

The ICI said net new cash flow to long-term mutual funds was estimated at $21.5 billion last month, compared with revised actual flows of $32.5 billion in January that were previously reported as $32.3 billion. Long-term mutual funds include stock, bond and income.
ICI said its monthly estimates are based on a survey of long-term funds that account for about 97 percent of long-term mutual fund assets.
Revisions to net new cash flows are provided to account for errors in new sales and redemption data reported to the institute, ICI said.
